 Rodgers: Al-Hilal is the toughest opponent we have faced since taking charge
 Thursday 22-10-2026 
 محمد أبو ريان 
 Rodgers stated during the press conference that Al-Hilal have high-level players, affirming his belief that the opponent is also aware of Al Qadisiyah's abilities, and expecting both sides to deliver an outstanding match.
 Al-Qadisiyah's coach emphasized the need to fight in every match to achieve the desired result, explaining that the Saudi Pro League does not feature easy matches, given the strength of competition among the teams.
 Rodgers noted that the pressure of matches imposes similar conditions on Al-Qadisiyah and Al-Hilal, pointing out that the coaching staff is focused on accelerating the players' return to physical readiness after each match.
 Preparation for Al-Hilal began immediately after the match against Al Taawoun, as the players headed to recovery in the dressing room right after the game, as part of the team's plan to get ready for the upcoming match.
 The top clash comes amid a fluctuating battle for the summit, with Al-Hilal regaining first place after a last-gasp victory over Al Hazm, before Al Qadsiah reclaimed the top spot with a thrilling win over Al Taawun in the dying seconds.
 Al-Qadisiyah lead the table with 25 points from 10 matches, while Al-Hilal sit in second place with 24 points from 9 encounters, making the match highly significant in the title race, with Al-Nassr, Al-Ittihad, and Al Ahly FC watching closely for the result.
 Brendan Rodgers, the head coach of Al Qadsiah, has described Al-Hilal as the strongest opponent he has faced since taking charge of the team, ahead of their anticipated clash in the 11th round of the Saudi Pro League.
